title: P1: context economy telemetry — per-section token attribution of every packet at build time, candidate vs presented, cross-role amplification, and a context view in the scorecard (no behaviour change)
spec:
One behaviour: every model invocation's packet is measured per section (deterministic chars // 4 plus a sha256 per section) and logged, so the scorecard can show how many tokens each section costs per role and how often the same section text is re-sent across a task's lineage. Nothing sent to any model changes.

Facts (verified 2026-09-22, main e8c4687): packets are assembled as named sections rendered "## <name>\n<body>": execute in spawn.py _packet_body (sections list at spawn.py:287-323, joined at :317), review in review_packet (spawn.py:435-488 via _section, diff bounded by a budget), spec_review_packet (:494-512) and scout_packet (:513-570) the same way; packet_run_meta (spawn.py:360-371) already parses the "packet v<hash> base <sha> sources ..." header and records chars, est_tokens, hash, version; packet_meta (:355) is stored on the task as packet_meta and copied into the run record; bus.log_run (bus.py:278-335) appends one JSON line per run to .orchestrator/runs/<date>.jsonl with role, tier, account, executor, task, tokens (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens), usd, duration, packet fields; scorecard.by_task/by_goal (scorecard.py:397-480) aggregate runs per task and goal using _tokens_of (:375) and attribution.lineage (attribution.py:96); the review prompt and execute prompt templates live in .orchestrator/prompts and are rendered by spawn.render (:101). Caps: execute packet 4800 chars (spawn.py:195-366), review diff ≤8000 chars, spec_review uncapped. Known duplication (leave it in place for this task; P4 removes it after the baseline): spec/acceptance/scope appear twice in the execute prompt (packet spawn.py:298-305 plus execute.md's literal lines).

Do:
1. spawn.py: `section_meta(text) -> dict` splits a rendered packet (or any prompt text) on lines starting with "## " into {section_name: {"chars", "est_tokens" (chars // 4), "sha256"}} plus "_preamble" for text before the first heading; packet_run_meta gains "sections": section_meta(text) and "presented_tokens" (sum), and the packet builders record "candidate_tokens": the est_tokens of every section BEFORE caps and budgets (the execute body before the 4800-char cap, the review diff before bounded_diff) so reduction_ratio = presented / candidate is available; when a builder cannot know the pre-cap size, candidate equals presented and the meta says "candidate_known": false. Also measure the prompt template around the packet: for each role, "instruction_tokens" = est_tokens of the rendered prompt minus the packet (render() output length minus packet length), recorded once per run.
2. bus.log_run: accept and persist `context` = {"sections": {...}, "presented_tokens", "candidate_tokens", "instruction_tokens", "packet_version"} on every run row that has a packet (execute, fix rounds, review, spec_review, scout, challenge, planner-decision when available). Old rows without it stay valid.
3. attribution/scorecard: a new module orchestrator/context_scorecard.py with build(root) -> rows per role: runs, avg presented_tokens, avg candidate_tokens, reduction_ratio, avg instruction_tokens, avg per-section tokens (top sections), plus per lineage root (attribution.lineage): amplification = sum of section tokens over all runs of the lineage / sum of tokens of unique (section sha256) across the lineage, and a repeated-sections list (which section names recur unchanged across roles); a `--context` view in `orchestrator scorecard` (cli.py) printing both tables. Rows without context are excluded and counted as "unmeasured".
4. Docs: docs/context-economy/01-telemetry.md explaining the fields, the chars // 4 convention, candidate vs presented, and amplification; .orchestrator/memory/architecture.md is NOT touched by this task (the Planner records it).
5. Tests: tests/test_spawn.py::test_section_meta_splits_named_sections (three sections plus preamble, chars and sha256 stable), tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_run_meta_reports_sections_and_presented_tokens, tests/test_spawn.py::test_review_packet_records_candidate_tokens_before_diff_budget (a long diff: candidate > presented), tests/test_bus.py::test_log_run_persists_context, tests/test_context_scorecard.py::test_amplification_counts_repeated_sections_once (three runs of one lineage sharing an identical spec section: amplification 3.0 for that section, 1.0 for unique ones), tests/test_context_scorecard.py::test_rows_per_role_and_unmeasured_count. All tests unittest.TestCase with the shared tests/_harness ORCH_ROOT.
Gate: .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0. No change to what any prompt contains.
acceptance: orchestrator scorecard --context prints per-role and per-lineage tables; docs/context-economy/01-telemetry.md exists; rendered prompts are byte-identical to before (no behaviour change)

spec_review_risks.issue: Item 3 defines amplification as one scalar per lineage root ('sum of section tokens over all runs of the lineage / sum of tokens of unique (section sha256) across the lineage'), but the acceptance test test_amplification_counts_repeated_sections_once wants a per-section breakdown ('amplification 3.0 for that section, 1.0 for unique ones'). Those are different data shapes (single ratio vs. a value per section name); an executor cannot satisfy both without the spec picking one.

instruction_tokens ('rendered prompt minus packet') requires two separate strings, but packet_run_meta(text) takes only one. Two real call sites feed it something other than a bare packet: _run() line 116 'task.get("packet_meta") or packet_run_meta(args[-1])' and start() line 334 'packet_meta if packet_meta is not None else packet_run_meta(prompt)' both fall back to the FULL rendered prompt (packet + trailing template text like 'Spec:', 'Acceptance:', 'Tests:'), and this fallback is not an edge case: orchestrator/mcp.py's codex() and codex_reply() tools -- the tools this repo's own CLAAUDE.md tells the Planner to call directly -- invoke executor.start(task_id, prompt) and executor.reply(task_id, delta) with no packet_meta at all. Once section_meta splits on '## ' headings, the trailing non-packet instruction text (no heading of its own) gets silently appended into the packet's last section body, corrupting that section's chars/est_tokens/sha256 and inflating presented_tokens for the primary Codex execute path. reply()'s resume branch is worse: args[-1] is just the repair delta (not a packet at all), so packet_run_meta(args[-1]) parses garbage when task.get('packet_meta') is falsy. None of the listed acceptance tests exercise executor.py or mcp.py, so a wrong implementation here ships silently.

attribution.lineage (attribution.py:96-108) only chains a task id through its own fix_round_for predecessors -- it does not link a spec_review task, its execute task, and that execute's review task, which are three separate task ids with three separate lineage roots. The facts paragraph names the motivating duplication as spec/acceptance/scope text resent across spec_review, execute, and review (the P4 target) -- exactly the case attribution.lineage-based grouping will NOT capture, since those live under different lineage roots. Grouping by task['parent'] (goal id) would capture it; grouping by attribution.lineage as specified will not.
